pr_summary: Add new NumberListAlignment enum setting to replace DontJustifyNumbers boolean. The new enum supports four modes: Left, Right, Decimal, and Normalize for aligning numeric values in JSON arrays and table-like structures.
environment_management: dotnet SDK (uses .NET 6.0 for tests, netstandard2.0 for library)
special_system_dependencies: .NET SDK 6.0 or later required for building and testing
patch_file_cues: New NumberListAlignment enum with Left, Right, Decimal, Normalize modes
Replacement of DontJustifyNumbers boolean with NumberListAlignment enum
Changes to TableTemplate.cs for number alignment logic
CLI argument change from -j|--no-justify to -j|--justify with values l/r/d/n
Web UI settings panel updated to use dropdown instead of checkbox
test_file_cues: Tests/NumberFormattingTests.cs - new tests for LeftAlign, RightAlign, DecimalAlign, NormalizeAlign
Test removed: DontJustifyOptionRespected (replaced by new alignment tests)
platform_constraint_evidence: Solution file (.sln) and csproj files are platform-agnostic
No Windows-specific APIs or MSVC dependencies in touched files
notes: The fix replaces a simple boolean DontJustifyNumbers with a more flexible NumberListAlignment enum offering four alignment modes. The main changes are in Formatter.cs, TableTemplate.cs, and FracturedJsonOptions.cs. Tests verify the new alignment modes produce correct output. This is a cross-platform .NET project that can be built and tested on Linux with the .NET SDK.
